verdict.rationale: Isaac Sim documents its own programmatic surfaces: Python namespace packages for composing the app, standalone scripts that control robots and environments, ROS 2 services for loading worlds, spawning entities and stepping simulations, and headless operation for automated workflows. Nothing in the evidence states that these APIs match everything the GUI can do. The 404 OpenAPI probe matters little for a Python/ROS-based simulator, and it does not contradict the claim. Missing for 10: an explicit statement or documentation of UI-to-API feature parity, a complete API reference showing coverage of GUI functions (scene assembly, materials, sensor setup), and independent hands-on corroboration that UI workflows can be fully scripted.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Isaac Sim provides several Python namespace packages that allow you to compose an Isaac Sim app by parts using a Python package manager (for example: pip).
Write your first standalone script to control robots and environments.
Use ROS 2 services and actions to load worlds, spawn entities, and step simulations.
deploy easily with standalone headless operation, from workstation to data center.
developers can build custom OpenUSD-based simulators, integrate framework capabilities into existing testing and validation pipelines, or automate workflows.
